description: One section of a periodic report: what it is called, where its numbers come from, and whether the report can be called finished without it. `data_source` names a tool on this site rather than describing a spreadsheet, which is what lets a report skeleton be generated with each section already pointing at the thing that fills it.

fields.description: The section's key — 'Results of Operations', 'Liquidity and Capital Resources', 'Segment Information'. Stable, because it is what a generated skeleton is keyed on across periods.
fields.label: Section Name

fields.description: Order in the report. Lower first. The default leaves room either side so inserting a section between two others does not mean renumbering the set.
fields.label: Sequence

fields.description: Whether the report is incomplete without it. An optional section that nobody wrote is a choice; a required one that nobody wrote is a gap, and the skeleton generator reports the two differently.
fields.label: Required

fields.description: The heading as it prints, in English. Falls back to the section name when empty.
fields.label: Label (EN)

fields.description: The heading in Spanish, for a reader who works in it. Empty means the English is served and the gap is REPORTED rather than hidden — see the Reporting Template docstring on why a half-translated document is worse than an untranslated one.
fields.label: Label (ES)

fields.description: WHICH TOOL ON THIS SITE FILLS THIS SECTION — 'get_cash_flow_summary', 'compute_all_kpis', 'generate_segment_report'. Named rather than described, so generate_quarterly_report_skeleton can hand somebody a section that already says where its numbers come from. Free text on purpose: a source that is a spreadsheet or a person is a real answer and refusing to record it would just mean it went unrecorded.
fields.label: Data Source

fields.description: What this section is for, and what belongs in it.
fields.label: Description

name: Reporting Template Section
